lesson.title: Sending Messages with Light and Sound
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: You've learned about light and sound separately. Did you know people use both of them to send messages, every single day?

Think about a traffic light — red, yellow, and green light signals tell drivers what to do without a single word. A doorbell uses sound to tell you someone is at the door. A fire alarm uses a loud sound (and often a flashing light too!) to warn people of danger. Can you think of one more way light or sound sends a message in your everyday life?
Light and sound aren't just things we notice — people use them on purpose to communicate important information. Tomorrow we'll investigate materials and how they interact with light.

objectives: Identify real examples of light and sound used to send information or signals (traffic lights, doorbells, alarms)
Explain in simple words why a signal (light or sound) can communicate a message without words
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child if they've ever seen a traffic light and what each color means.
2. Introduce the idea that light and sound can send messages without words.
3. Discuss a doorbell (sound) and a fire alarm (sound plus often light) as more examples.
4. Brainstorm one more real-life example together.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each example and talk through what message it sends.
6. Close by asking why a flashing light or loud sound might work better than words in an emergency.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the traffic light example, since it's likely the most familiar
Ready for more: discuss Morse code or another historical example of using light/sound patterns to send messages over distance
For a child who enjoys role play, act out being a crossing guard or traffic light using the three colors
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a vocabulary tracing and discussion activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct word tracing. Check that the child can explain what message each signal sends.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Recognizing that light and sound are used intentionally to communicate information is a core Grade 1 application of the NGSS 1-PS4 standard, connecting the abstract science of light/sound to real, familiar technology.
